<reason>CON won the central clash on third-party consent. PRO's lock-in case was strong but CON answered it with turnover, multi-homing, and narrow bans, while PRO never resolved the privacy-or-portability dilemma: unilateral transfer exports others without consent, reciprocal transfer leaves the mover alone. CON's typed-address vs platform-built-graph and fungible-dollars vs other-people distinctions dismantled the phone/email/banking analogies, and exposed PRO's late shift to ongoing federation as beyond one-time transfer.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's privacy-or-portability fork in R1/R2 — if links need acceptance the mover lands alone, if not 400 strangers are bulk-exported — which survived PRO's pointer/interoperability answer and framed the closing choice as lock-in vs leak-out.</best_rebuttal>
